answer: Copper-trace registration: each identity bid must join a pending pool tagged with a disclosed prior interaction record. If two bids share a source record or a device fingerprint lineage, the pool flags them and voids both. Yarrow-scored audit sampling then rechecks a random fraction each epoch, voiding flagged clusters. Attacker cost: every duplicate needs a genuinely distinct record chain, so forgery scales linearly; a single river of reused traces voids whole batches, wasting all registration effort spent on them.
